title: Brazilian rhythm: Joao Gilberto and Carmen Miranda
summary: Gil praises Brazilian music, which he first heard on Joao Gilberto's records.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: So that came from Brazil really. Originally you know. The Brazilian rhythm is so beautiful it's like a tree it just grew organically you know. The mixture of things however it came up and when you hear Brazilian rhythm, of course now all the rock music it's automatically there patterns and the whole thing. But Brazilian rhythm is full of sunshine.
Well were you there? How did you first get close to it?
Joao Gilberto. I got those records a long time ago, on the Odeon label.
Do you see a kind of Afro-Brazilian thing there?
Well Brazilian music is African music really. That's what I mean by it grew like a tree organically. African, Portuguese romantic like the romantic European, Spanish, Portuguese and Indian you know.

And it's blended together and it's been played down there so much, all day long, all week long, all month, all year long, all decade long, right? It's been played down there so much that actually the quality comes from quantity But you can't (go up to people always and say?) all that isn't possible and all that, it's not true. Quality is necessary. And quantity is necessary for quality. When you get it all together and that's ............ Anyway, that came out of that, that this Indian rhythm came out of it.

Even when Carmen Miranda came here thirty years ago with that little group it was a knockout. Nobody never heard anything like that. That lively way she had of coming on. Too much. Now that's the big thing, that's....... Brazil took the top song that was here, brought to a certain point here by the show composer like Cole Porter and Rodgers and Hart and Gershwin and Kern and Harold Arlen. people like that. They took that song when they began to go back here to the country music you know, when they started going into that, they took it over. Started writing those song. I hear it, the parts that have come from this music here, but it's also beautifully and artistically
